The Integrated Global Action Plan for the Prevention and Control of Pneumonia and Diarrhoea (GAPPD) aims to end preventable child deaths from these diseases by 2025. It proposes a cohesive approach that integrates critical services and interventions to create healthy environments, promote protective practices, and ensure access to proven preventive and treatment measures for every child. 4. Pneumonia and diarrhoea remain major killers of children under five, accounting for 29% of all deaths in this age group and resulting in the loss of 2 million young lives annually. Proven interventions exist to address these diseases, but services are often fragmented, and those most at risk are not being reached. 5. Effective interventions include exclusive breastfeeding for six months, vaccines against Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae type b, rotavirus, measles, and pertussis, as well as oral rehydration salts (ORS) and zinc supplementation for diarrhoea treatment. However, coverage of these interventions remains insufficient. 6. The GAPPD emphasizes the need for an integrated approach to address pneumonia and diarrhoea in a coordinated manner. It provides a roadmap for national governments and partners to plan and implement strategies for prevention and control, with a focus on engaging all relevant stakeholders, including frontline healthcare providers and communities. 7. The Protect, Prevent, and Treat framework is central to the GAPPD strategy. It includes promoting good health practices such as exclusive breastfeeding and vitamin A supplementation, preventing illness through vaccines and improved hygiene, and treating sick children with appropriate care, including antibiotics, ORS, and oxygen. 8. The GAPPD sets ambitious but achievable goals for 2025, including reducing pneumonia mortality in children under five to fewer than 3 per 1,000 live births, reducing diarrhoea mortality to fewer than 1 per 1,000 live births, and achieving 90% coverage of relevant vaccines and case management interventions. 9. The plan also highlights the importance of universal access to safe drinking water, sanitation, and clean energy technologies in healthcare facilities and homes by 2030. These measures are essential for creating a healthy environment and reducing the burden of pneumonia and diarrhoea. 10. To achieve these goals, governments and partners are encouraged to develop clear country-level strategies, prioritize interventions, and use data to identify and target high-risk groups. Coordination of implementation efforts and monitoring progress through common indicators are also critical components of the GAPPD approach.
